purpose: Bind the first Talos/vfkit/CAPI/Kamaji substrate slice to an executable, non-mutating contract matrix so workers can validate local Talos smoke, Cloudflare Access posture, CAPI/Argo CD/Kamaji integration and the managed-Kubernetes product surface without implying live cluster or hardware provisioning.

ADR-0370.authority_use: local production-fidelity Talos smoke and known Kata-on-Apple-Silicon gap

ADR-0371.authority_use: Cloudflare Tunnel L4 TCP plus Cloudflare Access control-plane posture

ADR-0375.authority_use: Talos installation media, Cluster API, ClusterResourceSet, and per-cell Argo CD fleet substrate

ADR-0376.authority_use: managed-Kubernetes two-tier product surface, Kamaji hosted default, and dogfood tenant-zero scope

ADR-0378.authority_use: canonical local vfkit plus Talos substrate smoke and colima retirement posture

can_claim_now: The TALOS-001 substrate slice is specified as a contract matrix in this dedicated spec.
The four first-slice surfaces have source ADRs, source paths, acceptance hooks, and non-claims.
cannot_claim_yet: local vfkit Talos cluster smoke has not been executed by this slice
Cloudflare Access service-token denial and tunnel health have not been executed by this slice
CAPI providers, ClusterResourceSet, Argo CD, and Kamaji controllers have not been installed by this slice
managed-Kubernetes product microservices are not promoted to runtime or public SLA by this slice

required_contract: vfkit plus Talos is the canonical local substrate; colima is retired as the active cluster target.
The operator config home is ~/.oya/talos-local with kube context admin@oya-local.
Talos remains immutable/API-driven with no SSH troubleshooting path.
Kata cloud-hypervisor on Apple Silicon is treated as a known local gap when the inner VMM cannot create a microVM; non-Kata substrate smoke can still pass.
acceptance: A future live smoke records talosctl and kubectl evidence against admin@oya-local.
The smoke distinguishes the known Apple-Silicon Kata gap from the health of the Talos/Cilium substrate.
No local smoke stores talosconfig, kubeconfig, machine secrets, or PKI material in git.
verification: future hardware/local evidence: kubectl config current-context == admin@oya-local and Talos node/Cilium/cloud-ci pods are observed from the canonical config home
non_claims: This slice does not boot vfkit, create a VM, run talosctl, or run kubectl against a live cluster.
This slice does not claim Kata workload readiness on Apple Silicon.

required_contract: OpenTofu owns only the Cloudflare edge root, not the cluster fleet.
The control-plane access posture is Cloudflare Tunnel as L4 TCP passthrough to the apiserver VIP, preserving apiserver mTLS end-to-end.
Cloudflare Access must front k8s.oyatie.dev with least-privilege service-auth and optional human SSO/WARP policy.
Tunnel, Access, connector, and service-token secrets remain in Keychain/OpenBao or equivalent custody, never git.
acceptance: Future live verification proves tokenless access is denied at Cloudflare Access before the apiserver and service-token access preserves client-certificate mTLS.
Future connector health evidence proves outbound-only cloudflared connectivity with no public inbound port.
verification: future edge evidence: cloudflared /ready healthy, tunnel connection count, Access tokenless deny, and kubeconfig client cert success through local cloudflared access tcp
non_claims: This slice does not run tofu plan/apply or modify Cloudflare resources.
This slice does not commit or inspect Cloudflare credentials, tunnel tokens, service-token material, talosconfig, kubeconfig, or private keys.

required_contract: Cluster API initializes Talos, OCI, AWS, and Metal3 providers on the management control plane; it is not a kind-only bootstrap path.
ClusterResourceSet installs Cilium and Argo CD bootstrap material into labelled clusters, while Argo CD CRDs travel through Talos extraManifests to avoid the ConfigMap size ceiling.
Per-cell Argo CD owns app delivery by pull model after the CAPI/Talos cluster exists.
Kamaji is additive to ADR-0375 as the hosted-default CAPI control-plane provider; dedicated premium clusters continue through Talos control-plane providers.
acceptance: A future live integration run records provider readiness, ClusterResourceSet render/apply evidence, Argo CD root Application health, and Kamaji TenantControlPlane reconciliation evidence.
The hosted and dedicated tiers share CAPI/Argo lifecycle semantics and differ only by control-plane placement.
verification: future live evidence: clusterctl describe, rendered CRS artifacts, Argo CD Synced/Healthy, and Kamaji TenantControlPlane Ready
non_claims: This slice does not install CAPI providers, Argo CD, Cilium, or Kamaji.
This slice does not claim hosted-tier control planes are ready for production use.

required_contract: The managed-Kubernetes surface remains four flat single-concern services: cluster-lifecycle, tenant-quota, control-plane-host, and SLA-observability.
Dogfood tenant-zero uses the same cluster-CRUD and control-plane-host flow as future customers; no internal bypass is permitted.
Hosted is the default tier via Kamaji; dedicated/sovereign Talos spoke remains premium.
Billing, public SLA, DPIA, and external multi-tenant GA remain deferred until separately authorized.
acceptance: Future product integration evidence shows cluster create/admit paths call quota and control-plane host seams before reporting managed-cluster status.
Future SLA-observability evidence distinguishes target SLO metadata from measured public SLA claims.
verification: future product evidence: cluster-lifecycle contract replay, quota deny/fail-closed tests, control-plane-host TenantControlPlane handle, and SLA observation read model
non_claims: This slice does not promote managed-Kubernetes APIs to general availability or a publicly committed SLA.
This slice does not mutate service code, tenant data, billing, quota state, or live control planes.

path_conflict_policy.generated_file_policy: No generated JSON or generated faces are edited by this slice.
